prospective_statement: Every relation, domain, refusal, bound and acceptance criterion in this file was derived from pinned source before any R3 or R2 numerical observation for Slice 2B. No mx.dequantize, mx.quantized_matmul, native bridge call or other numerical MLX operation was executed while drafting it. Fixture inputs were generated by a stdlib-only deterministic generator whose only arithmetic classifies inputs against this domain; nothing predicted or observed an MLX output. Every bound is prospective and frozen before observation once the owner accepts this file.

correction_policy.rule_1: An observation that exceeds a bound, violates an exact invariant, or fails any acceptance criterion is a FAIL. It is recorded against the original criteria of the contract version under which it was observed and is retained permanently.
correction_policy.rule_2: Any revision of a bound, a domain, a refusal, an assumption or an acceptance criterion is a new, separately identified contract version (new schema version string and file hash) that must be independently reviewed and explicitly authorized by the owner before any renewed qualification run.
correction_policy.rule_3: No appended entry, correction, erratum or replacement contract may convert a recorded failure into a pass, and no threshold is moved in place. A renewed qualification under a revised contract is a new run with its own evidence; the earlier failure remains a failure of the earlier version.
correction_policy.rule_4: The qualification report binds the sha256 of this contract file, the fixture manifest and the generator; a report produced under a different contract version cannot satisfy this version's acceptance criteria.

OP-IMPORT-META: exact import of scales/biases in F16, BF16 or F32 as MLX float16, bfloat16 or float32 arrays of the stored shape
OP-CAST: the bridge's own widening of F16/BF16 scales and biases to float32 (mlx_astype on the explicit GPU stream)
OP-DQ: mlx_dequantize, affine, bits {4,8}, group {32,64,128}, metadata F16/BF16/F32, output in the metadata dtype, GPU stream, inside domain D-DQ

OP-QMM: mlx_quantized_matmul, non-gathered, transpose=true ONLY (y = x @ W^T, W stored [N, K*bits/32], the Safetensors [out, in] layout), x float32 ONLY, metadata already float32 (widened by OP-CAST when stored as F16/BF16), GPU stream, inside domains D-GEOM and D-NUM
scope.production_relevance: Planner census fact (2026-09-23): both target checkpoints use only bits {4,8} x group 64 x BF16 scales/biases. The frozen population includes group-64/BF16 cases for both bit widths (flagged production_relevant) and keeps groups 32 and 128.

the CPU backend of either operation
any real-checkpoint payload and any production-geometry claim: small-fixture qualification is not production-geometry qualification

scope.packed_weight_path: OP-QMM consumes the packed U32 weight tensor directly: the imported U32 array is passed to mlx_quantized_matmul unchanged as `w` (operations.OP-QMM.mlx_c_call). Only scales and biases -- 1/group_size of the weight's logical element count -- are promoted to float32, by the exact bridge cast OP-CAST. The weight is never expanded to a float32 tensor on the QMM path: MLX builds the primitive inputs as {astype(x), w, astype(scales), astype(biases)} without casting w (MLX312:mlx/ops.cpp:4509-4512), and the kernels decode codes transiently (registers in the vector family; 32-wide tiles in threadgroup memory in the matrix family, MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/kernels/quantized.h:571-690). OP-DQ is a separate qualified operation and is not a preprocessing step of OP-QMM.

domains.principle: Domains that the bound derivation cannot cover are REFUSED by the bridge before any MLX call, each by a named refusal id, in the frozen order of `refusals.order`. Fixtures that probe a guard expect that refusal, never a numerical result.

D-GEOM.applies_to: OP-QMM; for OP-DQ the constraints rows >= 1, rows <= 16384, 1 <= K <= 16384 (K >= group via R-META), K % group == 0 and every tensor dimension >= 1 apply

constraints.all_dims: every dimension of every tensor (x, w, scales, biases) is >= 1 (R-EMPTY-DIM)
constraints.K: K = packed_cols*32/bits; group_size <= K <= 16384; K % group_size == 0 (K >= 1 is R-EMPTY-DIM; with K >= 1, R-META's packed*32 == groups*group*bits and groups >= 1 imply K >= group_size)
constraints.N: 64 <= N <= 16384 and N % 64 == 0 (N >= 1 is R-EMPTY-DIM; N >= 1 with N % 64 == 0 gives N >= 64)

justification.caps: K, N <= 16384 and M <= 4096 were set by the planner. They cover the hidden size 6144 recorded for the F017 target (REPO:docs/architecture/reviews/evidence/f017-native-bounded-p1-checkpoint-plan-audit-v1.json) and expert/intermediate dimensions below 16384. The exact module dimensions of the F020 target checkpoints are not in pinned repository sources (U17): the metadata census must confirm that every quantized module the product will send to OP-QMM has K, N <= 16384 and N % 64 == 0; a module outside (for example a vocabulary projection with N = 154880) is outside v1 geometry and is refused.
justification.N_mod_64: review F5: qmv_quad dispatches ceil(N/64) threadgroups of 64 output rows (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp:193-199) and loads sl[0]/bl[0] before its out_vec_size test (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/kernels/quantized.h:729-738). With N % 64 == 0 every row index row*8 + out_row (<= tid.y*64 + 63) is < N, so every scale, bias and weight load is in bounds: the tail case does not arise. The same alignment makes qmv's general path use full tiles (quantized.h:919-973, taken when N >= 8), makes qmm_t and qmm_t_splitk aligned (quantized.cpp:725, 826: aligned = N % 32 == 0) and keeps qmv_fast's bn = 8 tiles complete. The source hazard stays recorded (U18) for any future relaxation.
justification.caps_census_addendum: Data addendum 2026-09-23 (no bound, domain value or refusal changed): the Slice 2A metadata census of both target checkpoints is classified against D-GEOM in source-pins-slice2.json#production_geometry. The caps are inclusive (K <= 16384, N <= 16384). Out of v1 geometry: vocabulary projection and embedding (N = 154880 > 16384), the Flash indexer.weights_proj (N = 32, N % 64 != 0) and direct execution of every stacked rank-3 tensor (switch_mlp gate/up/down, embed_q, unembed_out: refused by R-WDTYPE; gather/stacked dispatch deferred); each individually selected rank-2 expert or per-head plane of those tensors fits D-GEOM, but plane extraction and its execution qualification are future work outside this slice. At the inclusive boundary: GLM-5.3 self_attn.o_proj (bits 8, packed [6144, 4096], scales [6144, 256], logical [6144, 16384]: K = 16384 exactly), Flash self_attn.o_proj in layers 3,7,...,43 (logical [4096, 16384]) and q_b_proj in both checkpoints (N = 16384). Correction note: an earlier planner expectation that some o_proj might exceed K = 16384 was a reporting error; the census shows K = 16384 exactly; no bound was changed to reconcile it.

D-GEOM.gamma_validity: Every gamma exponent n used under D-GEOM satisfies n*u <= 1/8, so gamma_n = n*u/(1-n*u) is well defined and gamma_n <= (8/7)*n*u <= 2*n*u. Largest exponents: qmm_t K+3 <= 16387; qmm_t_splitk Kp+sk+3 <= max over 2<=sk<=512 of K/sk+sk+3 <= 8197; qmv 8-bit K/4+5 <= 4101; qmv_fast 4-bit K/16+17 <= 1041, 8-bit K/8+9 <= 2057; qmv_quad K/4+5 <= 37. n_max = 16387, n_max*u = 9.77e-4 <= 1/8. The ambiguous-band maximum is over two of these, each valid. gamma64 exponents (K+1, 2K+4 <= 32772) are far below 2^50.

int32_intermediates.statement: Every signed-int / 32-bit index expression on the qualified paths is bounded under D-GEOM (and the DQ rows cap) by 2^28 < 2^31-1:

list.expr: out_row*in_vec_size_w in bytes (qmv_fast, qmv; in_vec_size_w = K*bytes_per_pack/pack_factor)
K_w = K*bytes_per_pack/pack_factor; wl += y_col*K_w; scales += y_col*K_g (qmm_t)
int B = out.size()/M/N; int M = x.size()/K
dequantize: offset/oindex/gindex as size_t; nthreads vs UINT_MAX
MLX shapes and MLX-C shape arguments are int
list.max: every dim <= 2^14 except none; element counts <= 2^28

D-GEOM.lower_bounds_note: Every lower bound is enforced before MLX is called and before any bridge expression divides by a dimension: R-EMPTY-DIM precedes R-META, R-XSHAPE and R-GEOMETRY in the refusal order, and the bridge computes M_eff as a product of x dims, K as packed*32/bits and groups via multiplication checks. Upstream divisions by dimensions such as out.size()/M/N (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp:191, 249, 714) are therefore never reached with a zero dimension.

constraints.finite: x, scales, biases contain no NaN or infinity (R-NONFINITE)
constraints.no_subnormal_operands: x (float32), scales and biases (in their stored dtype) contain no subnormal value (R-SUBNORMAL)
constraints.magnitude: every nonzero |x|, |s|, |b| lies in [2^-32, 2^32] (R-DOMAIN-X-RANGE, R-DOMAIN-META-RANGE); zeros of either sign are admitted

lemma_L.statement: Let every operand of a binary32 operation be an integer multiple of 2^-L with L <= 126 (a product's exact value is then a multiple of 2^-(L1+L2), which must itself satisfy the bound). If the exact result v lies within the finite float32 range -- under D-NUM every exact intermediate satisfies |v| <= 2^78, far below max_f32 = (2 - 2^-23)*2^127, so RN(v) cannot overflow -- then under A-OPS(b),(c) the computed result is an integer multiple of 2^-L, it is exactly zero if v = 0, and otherwise its magnitude is >= 2^-L >= 2^-126 (normal). The power-of-two prescaling steps are not covered by this lemma but by A-OPS(e), whose exact normal quotients lie on the stated lattices.
lemma_L.proof: If v = 0, A-OPS(c) gives a zero. Otherwise 2^-126 <= 2^-L <= |v| <= 2^78 < max_f32, so A-OPS(b) applies and the result is RN(v), which is finite because |v| is below the overflow threshold. If ulp(RN(v)) >= 2^-L, RN(v) is a multiple of its ulp and hence of 2^-L. Otherwise |v| < 2^(24-L), so v = k*2^-L with |k| < 2^24 is exactly representable and RN(v) = v. RN is monotone and 2^-126 is representable, so |RN(v)| >= 2^-L.

consequences.lattices: Every admitted x, s, b is a float32 value (after OP-CAST) with exponent >= -32, hence a multiple of 2^-55. qmv family: x/2^j (j <= 12, MLX312:quantized.h:62-71) in 2^-67 Z with magnitude >= 2^-44 (normal); code products and A_c in 2^-67 Z; S_c in 2^-55 Z; s*A_c in 2^-122 Z; b*S_c in 2^-110 Z; r_c = s*A_c + b*S_c and all accumulations (per-thread, simd_sum, quad_sum) in 2^-122 Z. qmm_t / qmm_t_splitk: s/16 in 2^-59 Z with magnitude >= 2^-36 (MLX312:quantized.h:521-525); dequantized w in 2^-59 Z; x*w in 2^-114 Z; MMA sums and split-K reduction in 2^-114 Z. All L <= 122 <= 126: by lemma L no intermediate is subnormal, every nonzero intermediate is normal and every zero intermediate is exact.
consequences.no_overflow: Exact magnitudes: |x/2^j| <= 2^32; |masked code * x/2^j| <= 15*2^32; |A_c| <= 255*2^40 < 2^48; |S_c| <= 2^40; |s| <= 2^36/255 < 2^28.01 so |s*A_c| < 2^77; |b*S_c| <= 2^76; every chunk result and accumulation <= sum_k (|s|q+|b|)|x_k| <= 2^76; qmm: |w| <= 2^36, |x*w| <= 2^68, sums <= 2^76. Computed partial sums exceed exact ones by at most a factor (1 + gamma_n) < 1.001. Every intermediate therefore stays <= 2^78 (below the planner's 2^100 target and far below max_f32).
consequences.review_counterexamples: F1 vector (x = 2^-120) and F2 (x = 2^126) are refused by R-DOMAIN-X-RANGE; F1 matrix (s = 2^-126) by R-DOMAIN-META-RANGE; all three are frozen refusal fixtures.

constraints.no_subnormal_operands: no subnormal scale or bias in T (R-SUBNORMAL)
constraints.range: for every element: |s|*q + |b| <= 0.5*max_T (R-DQ-RANGE), checked exactly on the host
constraints.normal_results: for every element, the exact values P + b and RN_T(P) + b (P = s*q) are each either zero or of magnitude >= lambda_T (R-DQ-NORMAL), checked exactly on the host

D-DQ.consequences: P = s*q is zero or has |P| >= |s| >= lambda_T; RN_T(P) is normal or zero; each admitted evaluation -- RN_T(RN_T(P)+b) (separate), RN_T(P+b) (contracted), RN_T(RN_32(P+b)) (contracted in float32 then rounded) -- has an exact pre-rounding value that is zero or in [lambda_T, 0.5*max_T*(1+u_T)+...] <= max_T, so it rounds to a finite normal value or an exact zero (A-OPS(b),(c)). For F32 and BF16 metadata the magnitude constraint already implies range and normal_results (lattice 2^-55 resp. 2^-39); the checks are still performed. For F16 both are active. Review F3's example (s=144, q=229, b=32544: |s|q+|b| = 65520 > 32752) is a frozen R-DQ-RANGE fixture; an R-DQ-NORMAL probe (P + b = 2^-23) is frozen too.

A-OPS.a: Conversions: a conversion (float16/bfloat16 -> float32, float -> float of the same type, integer code in [0, 2^16) -> float) whose exact result is representable in the destination returns exactly that value, including the sign of zero.
A-OPS.b: Basic operations: +, -, * and (if the compiler contracts) fused multiply-add, applied to operands that are zero or normal, whose exact result is nonzero, finite and of magnitude >= lambda of the result type T, return RN_T(exact) (round-to-nearest, ties-to-even) -- or, for T in {float16, bfloat16} only, RN_T(RN_32(exact)). The second form is covered by u_star_T and exists only for OP-DQ.
A-OPS.c: Zeros: an operation whose exact result is zero returns a zero with the IEEE 754-2019 section 6.3 sign (product: exclusive-or of signs; x + y with both +0 is +0; x + (-x) is +0 under round-to-nearest).
A-OPS.d: Subnormals: no subnormal operand reaches any operation (inputs refused by R-SUBNORMAL; intermediates excluded by lemma L and D-DQ), and no subnormal result occurs inside the admitted domains, so flush-to-zero behaviour (U2) cannot affect a qualified result. Subnormal behaviour is observed only as recorded, non-gating data in FX-CAST.
A-OPS.basis: Kernels built with -fno-fast-math (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/kernels/CMakeLists.txt:18); JIT fastMathEnabled=false (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/device.cpp:556). Metal's arithmetic semantics are not pinned source; A-OPS is an assumption. If it fails, the derived bounds and invariants are void.
A-OPS.e: Power-of-two division: the kernels' divisions of a normal float32 value by an exact power of two -- x/16.0f, x/256.0f, x/4096.0f in load_vector (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/kernels/quantized.h:62-71, identical expressions in load_vector_safe 142-151) and scale/16 in the matrix dequantize helper (quantized.h:521-525) -- return the exact quotient whenever that quotient is a normal float32 value. Under D-NUM the quotient is always normal (|x/4096| >= 2^-44, |s/16| >= 2^-36, both <= 2^32). This is an ASSUMPTION about Metal arithmetic (whether the division is lowered to an exact reciprocal multiply, a correctly rounded divide, or otherwise); pinned lowering evidence was not obtained (U19). No runtime probe is added, because it would be a numerical observation.

assumptions.A-SIMD: simd_sum and quad_sum are compositions of binary32 additions satisfying A-OPS(b),(c), in an unknown order (MLX312:quantized.h:742, 809, 913, 969; U4).
assumptions.A-MMA: simdgroup_multiply_accumulate on 8x8 float32 tiles is a composition of binary32 multiplies and adds or fused multiply-adds satisfying A-OPS(b),(c), in an unknown order (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/kernels/steel/gemm/mma.h:205, 446, 476-478, 526; U5).

A-NONAX.statement: NAX kernels are never executed by a qualified call.
A-NONAX.derivation: qmm routes to qmm_nax only when is_nax_available() && transpose && K % 64 == 0 && (env::enable_tf32() || x.dtype() != float32) (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp:695-712; qmm_splitk reaches it only through its qmm fallback, 802-805). x is always float32 here. enable_tf32() = atoi(getenv("MLX_ENABLE_TF32")) cached in a function-local static (MLX312:mlx/utils.h:171-174; mlx/utils.cpp:289-295). With MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 in the child's environment at process start, the branch is unreachable by source on any hardware or build.
A-NONAX.runtime_assertion: The child asserts at startup, before any MLX-C call, that getenv("MLX_ENABLE_TF32") == "0" and that MLX_METAL_GPU_ARCH, MLX_MAX_OPS_PER_BUFFER and MLX_MAX_MB_PER_BUFFER are unset; otherwise it refuses (R-NAX) and exits with the dedicated status. It records the device_info architecture string, the parsed generation (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/device.cpp:485-497), nax_capable_hardware (device.cpp:828-847), and whether the loaded mlx.metallib contains a kernel name with '_nax_' (byte scan of the loaded file).

derivation_map.N-CAST-WIDEN: A-OPS(a) only (every zero/normal F16 and BF16 value is exactly representable in float32)
derivation_map.N-DQ-CODES: A-OPS(a) (code -> T exact, 1.0 exact), A-OPS(b) (q*1 = q and q + 0 = q are exact representable nonzero results, hence returned exactly for q >= 1, contracted or not), A-OPS(c) (q = 0: (+0)*1 = +0, +0 + +0 = +0, fma(1, +0, +0) = +0)
derivation_map.N-QMM-ZERO: A-OPS(c) with A-SIMD/A-MMA: every exact intermediate of an all-zero x row is zero
derivation_map.N-DQ-BOUND, N-QMM-BOUND: A-OPS(a),(b),(c),(d),(e), lemma L / D-DQ, A-SIMD, A-MMA, A-NONAX

OP-IMPORT-U32.mlx_c_call: mlx_array_new_data(words, shape, 2, MLX_UINT32) (MLXC:mlx/c/array.cpp:236-252; uint32 case 177-180): copying constructor; the returned handle's ctx must be non-null

invariant.statement: after eval + synchronize + host read-back through the Evaluated typestate, bytes equal the source bit for bit; dtype MLX_UINT32; shape == stored shape

OP-IMPORT-META.mlx_c_call: mlx_array_new_data(values, shape, rank, MLX_FLOAT16 | MLX_BFLOAT16 | MLX_FLOAT32) (MLXC:mlx/c/array.cpp:201-218)

invariant.statement: read-back bit-identical to the source for every element, exhaustively over all 65536 F16 and BF16 patterns (NaN payloads, signed zeros, subnormals, infinities included)

OP-CAST.mlx_c_call: mlx_astype(&res, meta, MLX_FLOAT32, gpu_stream) (MLXC:mlx/c/ops.h:161-165) for F16/BF16 metadata; for F32 metadata no cast is issued
OP-CAST.why: review F6: quantized_matmul's own casts, astype(scales, dtype) and astype(biases, dtype), are called WITHOUT the stream argument (MLX312:mlx/ops.cpp:4509-4512) and would resolve through default_stream(default_device()) (MLX312:mlx/utils.cpp:15-17, to_stream of an empty StreamOrDevice). The bridge therefore widens the metadata itself on the explicit GPU stream. MLX's astype returns its argument unchanged, creating no primitive, when the dtype already matches (MLX312:mlx/ops.cpp:258-261), so inside quantized_matmul all three astype calls (x is float32 too) are no-ops and every primitive in the QMM graph carries the explicit stream. A non-matching astype builds an AsType primitive (ops.cpp:262-267) evaluated by copy_gpu (MLX312:mlx/backend/gpu/primitives.cpp:28-33) as dst[i] = static_cast<float>(src[i]) (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/kernels/copy.h:30, 34).
OP-CAST.default_device_policy: Additionally the child sets the default device to GPU at startup (mlx_set_default_device, MLXC:mlx/c/device.h:74) and asserts before every op that mlx_get_default_device (device.h:70) reports MLX_GPU; no broadcast (w rank 2) or other default-stream op is reachable in v1.

invariant.statement: for every zero or normal finite F16 and BF16 bit pattern, the bridge's mlx_astype to float32 on the GPU stream returns exactly the host widening, bit for bit including the sign of zero
invariant.recorded_only: subnormal, infinity and NaN patterns are cast and recorded, not gated

checks.statement: output dtype == metadata dtype; shape [rows, K]
with scales = 1 and biases = +0, every output equals its code exactly (bit for bit, +0 for code 0); also execution canary E4

checks.derivation: separate: (P(1+d1) + b)(1+d2) with |di| <= u_star_T; contracted: <= u_star_T|w|; no absolute term because D-DQ excludes subnormal results and operands (A-OPS(d))
checks.no_exact_value_invariant: U1 (contraction) leaves three admissible results; none is claimed exactly

checks.statement: out is one of RN_T(RN_T(P)+b), RN_T(P+b), RN_T(RN_32(P+b)); recorded per element

checks.applies_to: OP-DQ cases carrying both rust_binary64_r1 and python_exact_r1 (59 cases); not the 18 codes_exact cases
checks.statement: for every element: |w_hat_R1_rust - w_exact| <= 2^-53 * |w_exact|, where w_hat_R1_rust = fl64(fl64(s*q) + b) is the Rust R1 binary64 value and w_exact = s*q + b is the exact rational
checks.derivation: s*q is exact in binary64 (at most 24 + 8 significand bits); one correctly rounded binary64 addition of exact operands has relative error <= 2^-53 (A-OPS is not involved: this is host binary64 arithmetic under IEEE 754)
checks.decision: exact rational comparison: w_hat is a binary64 value, hence a dyadic rational, and w_exact is a Fraction; no padding is used

OP-QMM.mlx_c_call: mlx_quantized_matmul(&res, x, w, scales_f32, biases_f32, transpose=true, {gs,true}, {bits,true}, "affine", gpu_stream) (MLXC:mlx/c/ops.h:809-819; ops.cpp:2585-2617); the public bridge API has no transpose parameter
OP-QMM.semantics: y = x @ W^T, W stored [N, K*bits/32], groups along K (MLX312:mlx/ops.cpp:131-132); output dtype float32; output shape x.shape with last dim N (4519-4520)

rules: L = get_qmv_batch_limit(K, N, arch) (quantized.cpp:83-126): suffix 'd': 32 / 18 / 12 for (K,N both <= 2048) / (both <= 4096) / otherwise; generation 13 or 14 otherwise: 14 / 10 / 6; any other generation: 18 / 12 / 10
M_eff < L: qmv_quad if K in {64,128} (1380); else qmv_fast if N % 8 == 0 and K % 512 == 0 (259); else qmv
M_eff >= L: qmm_splitk (1412-1419) with split_k = max(1, 512 div (ceil(N/32)*ceil(M_eff/32))), capped at K/group_size, decremented until K % (split_k*group_size) == 0; split_k <= 1 -> qmm_t (773-805)
kernel_selection_0_31_2.architecture_dependence: M_eff <= 5 -> vector family on every architecture; M_eff >= 32 -> matrix family on every architecture; 6 <= M_eff <= 31 -> either, by architecture. split_k is architecture-independent.
kernel_selection_0_31_2.identification: No kernel-reporting API exists. The family is derived deterministically from (M_eff, N, K, group_size, bits) and the recorded architecture string; the evidence records effective geometry, dtype, contiguity (always row-contiguous copies), L, split_k and the derived family per case.

checks.statement: an all-(+/-0) row of x yields +0 or -0 in every output of that row

checks.notation: u = 2^-24; gamma_n = n*u/(1-n*u); Phi = sum_k (|s|*q + |b|)*|x_k| per output element; y* exact

per_family.qmm_t_splitk: |y - y*| <= gamma_{Kp + sk + 3} * Phi, sk = split_k, Kp = K/sk (includes the float32 split-K reduction)

checks.derivation: qmv family: general form gamma_{v+C+1} with v inputs per thread chunk (K/4, 16 or 8, 8 or 4) and C = K/v chunks: v roundings in A_c (any order, with or without FMA), 2 for s*A_c + b*S_c, C-1 in the per-thread and lane accumulation (A-SIMD); S_c's v-1 roundings are dominated; power-of-two prescaling of x and of the masked code is exact (lemma L: results normal). qmm_t: 2 in the float32 dequantized weight, 1 in the product, K-1 additions (A-MMA). qmm_t_splitk: the same over Kp inputs, an identity float32 store, sk-1 reduction additions. The final static_cast<float> is the identity. No absolute (underflow) term: lemma L. No c_T terms: T = float32.
checks.ambiguous_band: for 6 <= M_eff <= 31 the bound is the maximum of the vector-family bound selected by (K, N, bits) and the matrix-family bound selected by split_k; both components are valid under D-GEOM

checks.statement: OP-QMM only: on every OP-QMM case carrying both references, for every output element: |y_R1_rust - y_exact| <= gamma64_{K+1}*Phi

acceptance_implementation.principle: Exactly one frozen decision algorithm per gate and reference kind. Where a case lists both references, BOTH decisions must pass. Implementation discretion is not permitted: the expressions below are the acceptance criteria.
acceptance_implementation.notation: fl(.) = one binary64 round-to-nearest-even operation; every constant written as a power of two is exact in binary64; P48 = 1 + 2^-48, M48 = 1 - 2^-48 (both exact in binary64). Padding rule: each padded quantity below is a binary64 expression containing at most 8 fl operations after the mathematically bounded quantity it approximates; their combined relative deviation is below 8*2^-53*(1 + 2^-50) < 2^-49.9, which one multiplication by P48 (upper estimates) or M48 (lower estimates), including that multiplication's own rounding, dominates. RN operations can round either way; the conservatism comes from this combined padding, not from the direction of any single rounding.
acceptance_implementation.coverage: From the frozen manifest: 298 cases carry the Rust binary64 R1 (all 239 accepted OP-QMM cases and the 59 accepted OP-DQ cases other than the unit-scale code cases); 296 cases carry the exact Python R1 (the 59 OP-DQ cases and the 237 OP-QMM cases with M_eff*N*K <= 2^21); every one of those 296 also carries the Rust R1. The 18 unit-scale code/canary cases carry only codes_exact. Import and cast cases carry byte_identity (8) and exact_host_widening (2).

G-QMM-EXACT (N-QMM-BOUND, exact Python R.inputs: y3 = the R3 float32 output (a dyadic rational); y* = sum_k (s*q + b)*x_k computed in fractions.Fraction from the stored bytes (metadata widened exactly); Phi = sum_k (|s|*q + |b|)*|x_k| in Fraction; n = the case's gamma exponent (for 6 <= M_eff <= 31 the larger of the two candidate families' exponents, as recorded in the manifest)
G-QMM-EXACT (N-QMM-BOUND, exact Python R.decide: pass iff |y3 - y*| <= (n / (2^24 - n)) * Phi, compared exactly in Fraction. No reference-error term (the reference is exact).

G-QMM-RUST (N-QMM-BOUND, Rust binary64 R.reference: w_k = fl(fl(s*q) + b) with s*q exact in binary64 (at most 24+8 significand bits); y1 = sequential binary64 sum over k of fl(w_k*x_k) (k ascending); Phi_hat = sequential binary64 sum over k of fl(fl(fl(|s|*q) + |b|)*|x_k|)
G-QMM-RUST (N-QMM-BOUND, Rust binary64 R.reference_error: |y1 - y*| <= gamma64_{K+1} * Phi and |Phi_hat - Phi| <= gamma64_{K+2} * Phi, gamma64_m = m*2^-53/(1 - m*2^-53)
G-QMM-RUST (N-QMM-BOUND, Rust binary64 R.B_lo: g = fl(fl(n*2^-24) / fl(1 - n*2^-24)) (n*2^-24 and 1 - n*2^-24 are exact); B_lo = fl(fl(fl(g * M48) * Phi_lo) * M48)
G-QMM-RUST (N-QMM-BOUND, Rust binary64 R.d_hi: d_hi = fl(fl(fl(|fl(y3 - y1)| * P48) + e_R1_hi) * P48)
G-QMM-RUST (N-QMM-BOUND, Rust binary64 R.decide: pass iff d_hi <= B_lo. Then |y3 - y*| <= |y3 - y1| + |y1 - y*| <= d_hi <= B_lo <= gamma_n * Phi. A fail is a FAIL.

G-DQ-EXACT (N-DQ-BOUND, exact Python R1).inputs: out = the R3 output element in T (dyadic rational); P = s*q and w = P + b exactly in Fraction; u_star_T exact rational (2^-24 for F32; 2^-11 + 2^-24 + 2^-35 for F16; 2^-8 + 2^-24 + 2^-32 for BF16)
G-DQ-EXACT (N-DQ-BOUND, exact Python R1).decide: pass iff |out - w| <= u_star_T*(1 + u_star_T)*|P| + u_star_T*|w|, compared exactly in Fraction

G-DQ-RUST (N-DQ-BOUND, Rust binary64 R1).reference: P_hat = fl(s*q) = s*q exactly (s has at most 24 significand bits, q at most 8); w_hat = fl(P_hat + b)
G-DQ-RUST (N-DQ-BOUND, Rust binary64 R1).reference_error: |w_hat - w| <= 2^-53 * |w| (one correctly rounded addition of exact operands); hence |w| >= |w_hat| / (1 + 2^-53) and |w| <= |w_hat| / (1 - 2^-53)
G-DQ-RUST (N-DQ-BOUND, Rust binary64 R1).constants: c1 = u_star_T*(1 + u_star_T), c2 = u_star_T; in binary64: c2 is exact (u_star_T has at most 25 significant bits); c1_lo = fl(fl(c2 * fl(1 + c2)) * M48)
G-DQ-RUST (N-DQ-BOUND, Rust binary64 R1).d_hi: d_hi = fl(fl(fl(|fl(out - w_hat)| * P48) + fl(|w_hat| * 2^-52)) * P48)  (the second term bounds |w_hat - w| <= 2^-53|w| <= 2^-53|w_hat|(1 + 2^-52))
G-DQ-RUST (N-DQ-BOUND, Rust binary64 R1).decide: pass iff d_hi <= B_lo, for every element. Then |out - w| <= |out - w_hat| + |w_hat - w| <= d_hi <= B_lo <= c1*|P| + c2*|w|.

G-DQ-CODES (N-DQ-CODES, codes_exact).decide: pass iff every output element is bit-identical to the T encoding of its code (code 0 -> +0). Exact equality only; no R1-bound decision applies to these 18 cases.

G-IMPORT and G-CAST.decide: N-IMPORT-*: byte equality of the read-back; N-CAST-WIDEN: bit equality with the host widening on zero/normal finite patterns

acceptance_implementation.both_references_rule: For every case whose manifest `references` lists both rust_binary64_r1 and python_exact_r1, the case passes only if BOTH the exact decision and the Rust decision pass.
acceptance_implementation.draft2_correction: draft.2 placed R1's error on the bound side (lenient). Since draft.3 it is on the distance side.

G-R1-SELF-QMM (N-R1-SELF, OP-QMM cases w.decide: for every output element: pass iff |y1 - y*| <= (K+1)*2^-53 / (1 - (K+1)*2^-53) * Phi, compared exactly in Fraction (y1 the Rust R1 binary64 value as a dyadic rational, y* and Phi exact)

G-R1-SELF-DQ (N-R1-SELF-DQ, OP-DQ cases.decide: for every element: pass iff |w_hat - w_exact| <= 2^-53 * |w_exact|, compared exactly in Fraction (w_hat the Rust R1 binary64 value as a dyadic rational, w_exact = s*q + b exact); no padding

acceptance_implementation.codes_exclusion: The 18 codes_exact cases have no R1 reference and no R1-bound decision; they are decided only by G-DQ-CODES and are excluded from B5.

refusals.principle: Checked by the bridge, in this order, before any MLX-C numerical call; the first failing check's id is returned as a typed error.

order.condition: context device not GPU, Metal unavailable, stream device not MLX_GPU, or default device not MLX_GPU
weight not U32 or not rank 2
any dimension of x, w, scales or biases equals 0 (M_eff = 0, N = 0, K = 0, zero metadata rows or groups); checked before any check that uses a dimension as a divisor
scales/biases dtype not in {F16, BF16, F32}, dtypes or shapes differ, rows differ from the weight, or packed_cols*32/bits != groups*group_size
x rank not in 1..3, or x.shape[-1] != K (zero dimensions are owned by R-EMPTY-DIM and are not part of this predicate)
D-GEOM violated for positive dimensions: K > 16384, N > 16384, M_eff > 4096, (N >= 1 and N % 64 != 0) for OP-QMM, (K >= 1 and K % group_size != 0); zero dimensions are owned by R-EMPTY-DIM
NaN or infinity in x, scales or biases
a subnormal x, scale or bias (all numeric ops, dequantize included)
a NORMAL x with |x| outside [2^-32, 2^32] (non-finite values are owned by R-NONFINITE, subnormal values by R-SUBNORMAL)
a NORMAL scale or bias with magnitude outside [2^-32, 2^32] (both ops)
sum over the finite values of a row of |x| exceeds 2^40
for a group whose scale and bias are zero or normal: |s|*255 + |b| > 2^36
OP-DQ: exact P + b or RN_T(P) + b nonzero with magnitude < lambda_T for some element

refusals.fixture_coverage: Every data-reachable id has at least one FX-REFUSE probe, and EVERY probe violates EXACTLY ONE evaluable guard -- its expected id -- asserted by the generator on every run including --check (manifest fields violated_guards and not_evaluable_guards). Every accepted case has every guard evaluable and satisfied. The review's literal F2 values (x = 2^126) necessarily violate both R-DOMAIN-X-RANGE and R-DOMAIN-ROWSUM and are represented by the single-guard probes ref-astra-f2-rowsum-in-range, ref-x-above-range and ref-astra-f1-vector-x-underflow. R-EMPTY-DIM probes: the review's exact R2-2 example (x [1,64], w [0,8], scales/biases [0,1]), M = 0, K = 0, and dequantize with empty metadata rows and with K = 0. R-NAX is exercised by a parent-level test.
refusals.guard_evaluation: The bridge evaluates the guards in `order` and returns the first violated id. For fixtures the generator evaluates EVERY guard independently (guard_results in the generator): value classes are disjoint (non-finite -> R-NONFINITE only, subnormal -> R-SUBNORMAL only, the range, row-sum, envelope and element guards read only zero/normal values), and a guard whose input precondition fails (e.g. metadata guards when R-META fails, x guards when x is not F32, K-dependent guards when the weight is not a rank-2 U32 tensor) is recorded as not evaluable in the manifest.
refusals.exactly_one_verification: Re-verified for draft.5 against the contract's own predicates: for all 37 FX-REFUSE probes the set of violated contract guards equals {expected id}. The structural predicates as worded here (R-EMPTY-DIM, R-META with the rational K = packed*32/bits, R-XSHAPE without a zero-dimension clause, R-GEOMETRY for positive dimensions) agree with the generator's guard_results on every probe (0 mismatches); for the six probes with not-evaluable guards (ref-x-f16, ref-x-bf16, ref-meta-dtype-mismatch, ref-meta-shape-mismatch, ref-weight-rank3, ref-weight-f32) an evaluation that ignores the preconditions finds no non-finite, subnormal or out-of-range value either. Under draft.4's R-XSHAPE wording ref-empty-m-zero and ref-empty-k-zero would have violated two guards; that is the R3-2 defect this revision removes.

required.check: GPU device and owned stream; stream device asserted MLX_GPU before every op; default device set to GPU at startup and asserted MLX_GPU before every op; every op receives the explicit stream

the Rust `Evaluated` typestate enforces mlx_array_eval(out) == 0, then mlx_synchronize(stream) == 0, then a host copy of the bytes through mlx_array_data_* (non-null); comparisons use only that copy. MLX-C does not itself prevent reading unevaluated data (mlx_array_data_* return array::data<T>() without an evaluation check: MLXC:mlx/c/array.cpp:517-524 and neighbours; MLX312:mlx/array.h:373-381); the typestate is the enforcement.

execution_evidence.thread_affinity: 0.31.2 command encoders are thread_local (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/device.cpp:809-822; eval.cpp:14-19); all MLX work of a child runs on one thread; contexts and arrays are !Send + !Sync

error_handling.handler: mlx_set_error_handler (MLXC:mlx/c/error.h:20-23) is called exactly once per process through a std::sync::Once, before the first context is created, with data = null and dtor = null (MLXC:mlx/c/error.cpp:20-34). Contexts never call it. The handler copies the message into a thread-local slot and returns; it never exits or unwinds. Rationale: MLX-C keeps the handler and its data in unsynchronized process globals (error.cpp:17-18).
error_handling.coexistence_policy: Inside the qualification child no other component may install an MLX-C error handler: the child links only the new crate and std; a static test asserts that the new crate contains exactly one mlx_set_error_handler call site (in its Once) and that no other workspace crate linked into the child calls it (crates/stream does not at the anchor).
error_handling.status_calls: every MLX-C call that returns int is checked; nonzero -> typed Rust error with the thread-local message; any result handle created by mlx_array_new() is freed (empty-handle free is a no-op, MLXC:mlx/c/private/array.h:49-53)
error_handling.empty_handle_checks: constructors without a status code are checked for an empty handle and for a set error slot: mlx_device_new_type (device.h:42), mlx_stream_new_device (stream.h:35), mlx_array_new_data (array.h:121), mlx_device_info_new; value accessors without status (mlx_array_dtype returns MLX_BOOL on error, MLXC:mlx/c/array.cpp:339-346; ndim, size, shape) are called only on handles proven non-empty and the error slot is checked after each; mlx_array_data_* and mlx_array_shape must return non-null

child_process.design: all native qualification runs in a child process with a fixed environment; the child writes a JSON report
parent_failure_conditions: exit by signal (reported with the signal number)
nonzero exit status (reported with the code)
child_process.watchdog: CHILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1800 (frozen). On expiry the parent sends SIGKILL, reaps the child with waitpid, and records an explicit TIMEOUT failure with the elapsed time; there is no retry.
child_process.residual_risk: a 0.31.2 GPU command-buffer fault is thrown inside a Metal completion handler (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/eval.cpp:21-28, 60-84); it is expected to terminate the child (U9) or may hang it; both become reported failures (signal/exit status or TIMEOUT), never a harness abort or a silent pass

ownership.model: NativeContext owns one mlx_device and one mlx_stream (Drop: mlx_synchronize, mlx_stream_free, mlx_device_free). NativeArray<'ctx> owns one mlx_array (copying import or op result); freed once in Drop; no Clone, raw accessor or into_raw.
invariants: L-ONCE: each handle freed exactly once
L-OUTLIVE: no array outlives its context
L-ERRFREE: error paths free created handles
